consecutive_difference_s.meaning: |L_{k+1} - L_k|. A CONSTANT offset cancels here, which is the quantity the sandwich audit of 12.6 item 4 actually forms. Drift, quantisation and varying delivery delay do NOT cancel.

analysis.not_written_to_config: anchor.posting_latency_p95_s is left frozen. Root: do not silently replace the frozen tolerance.

rtt_monotonic_s.meaning: send to ack on ONE clock (local monotonic). A true duration.

server_minus_client_s.meaning: created_at minus the client send wall time. This is LATENCY PLUS CLOCK OFFSET, not latency. created_at has ONE SECOND resolution, so these values are quantised to whole seconds.

analysis.status_of_this_number: CALIBRATION EVIDENCE from a 20-posting empirical sample. NOT a guaranteed future worst-case bound.

authority: root 2026-09-22 02:49, reviews/live_load_root_decision_20260922_0237.md line 31: option (b), dedicated drill issue, finite 20 postings, amendment recorded before the first post

finding.consequence_for_the_frozen_tolerance: The pre-registered second term of the sandwich tolerance is p95 of posting latency. Taken literally from this sample it is 0.247 s -- SMALLER than the median round trip of 0.599 s, because flooring biases it downward by up to 1 s. The quantity the audit actually forms, |L_k+1 - L_k|, has p95 1.541 s: about six times larger. Using p95(L) would make the tolerance term smaller than the variation it exists to absorb. Both are small beside the 30 s base (30.25 s versus 31.54 s), so this is a definitional defect with a bounded practical effect, not a broken audit.
finding.headline: server_minus_client_s is mostly NEGATIVE (median -0.279 s, min -0.702 s). It is not a latency and must never be reported as one.
finding.not_acted_on: config.json anchor.posting_latency_p95_s is left null and frozen. Root: "Do not silently replace the frozen tolerance." Which definition the tolerance uses is root's ruling.
finding.why: GitHub floors created_at to whole seconds. A posting sent at wall time X.9 and stamped at server second floor(X + true_latency) can carry a created_at EARLIER than its own send time. The measured clock offset is small (+0.018 to +0.185 s, ANCHOR_CLOCK_PROBE.json), so flooring, not clock skew, dominates the sign.

limitations: A 20-posting empirical p95 is CALIBRATION EVIDENCE, not a guaranteed future worst-case bound (root, 2026-09-22 02:49).
All 20 postings fall inside 33 seconds of one quiet period; they do not sample GitHub latency across load regimes, times of day, or network conditions.
created_at has ONE SECOND resolution. No sub-second statement about posting latency can be made from it, in either direction.
Overlapping HTTP-Date intervals bound a clock OFFSET; they do not prove clock synchronization and none is claimed.
rtt_monotonic_s is the only one of the three quantities that is a true duration on a single clock.
what_it_does_not_establish: any live episode, model call or trial clearance
that a trial-time posting will behave like a drill-time posting
what_the_drill_establishes: 20 of 20 postings succeeded (HTTP 201) against the real repository, with server comment ids and created_at retained per posting, failures included by design.
The identifier scanner passed over all 20 bodies before any was posted -- the stated reason 12.4 item 10 requires the real repository.
The anchor posting path works end to end against the real remote with a mock chain carrying the real freeze-receipt field shapes.
why_superseded: v1 reported server_minus_client_s with n=0 and None percentiles. created_at is ISO 8601 and v1 parsed it with email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime, which reads RFC 2822; every parse raised and a bare except swallowed all twenty. v1 is retained because a deposited artifact is not deleted to hide a defect; its numbers for rtt_monotonic_s were and remain correct.
